props.name: Claim: The review concludes that Cu-based catalysts owe their CO2RR capabilit…

evidence.quote: its adsorption free energy for *CO (ΔG(*CO) ≈ 0.45 eV) falls within

props.statement: The review concludes that Cu-based catalysts owe their CO2RR capability to a moderate adsorption free energy of the *CO intermediate, quoted as ΔG(*CO) ≈ 0.45 eV, which stabilizes intermediates and enables C−C coupling without poisoning the sites.

props.name: Claim: The review states that Cu is the only metal that efficiently converts…

evidence.quote: a range of hydrocarbons and alcohols with high selectivity
Cu is the only metal capable of efficiently converting CO2

props.statement: The review states that Cu is the only metal that efficiently converts CO2 into a range of hydrocarbons and alcohols with high selectivity in CO2RR.

props.name: Claim: The review concludes that the high stability of the C=O bond, with a b…

evidence.quote: characterized by a bond dissociation energy of approximately 750

props.statement: The review concludes that the high stability of the C=O bond, with a bond dissociation energy it quotes as approximately 750 kJ·mol−1, creates a kinetic barrier and a high overpotential demand in electrocatalytic CO2 reduction.

props.name: Claim: The review concludes that electron-donating and electron-withdrawing e…

evidence.quote: at Cu active centers through synergistic inductive-conjugative coupling

props.statement: The review concludes that electron-donating and electron-withdrawing effects tune the electron cloud density at Cu active centers through inductive and conjugative coupling, and thereby the adsorption, activation barrier and pathway of CO2 reduction.

props.name: Claim: The review reports DFT evidence that the *CHO intermediate is stabiliz…

evidence.quote: *CHO intermediate can be stabilized via electronic interaction with the positively charged

props.statement: The review reports DFT evidence that the *CHO intermediate is stabilized by electronic interaction with the positively charged −NH3+ group of zwitterionic glycine adsorbed near Cu sites (Li et al., ref. 53).

props.name: Claim: The review reports DFT results (Wang et al., ref. 55) in which polar e…

evidence.quote: shift the Cu d-band center to strengthen *CO adsorption, lower the activation energy of

props.statement: The review reports DFT results (Wang et al., ref. 55) in which polar electron-donating groups of functionalized ionic liquids transfer electrons to the Cu surface, upshifting the Cu d-band center, strengthening *CO adsorption, lowering the *CO−*CO coupling barrier and suppressing HER, while non-polar −CH3 groups show negligible effect.

props.name: Claim: The review concludes that steric hindrance from long alkyl chains rest…

evidence.quote: prolongs their surface residence time, and raises the local CO

props.statement: The review concludes that steric hindrance from long alkyl chains restricts *CO diffusion, prolongs its surface residence time and raises the local CO concentration, promoting multi-carbon products (Li et al., ref. 62).

props.name: Claim: The review concludes that high-density single-atom site configurations…

evidence.quote: but also promote C−C coupling via synergistic effects between adjacent sites

props.statement: The review concludes that high-density single-atom site configurations promote C−C coupling through synergistic effects between adjacent sites, a mechanism it calls widely confirmed for C2 product formation over Cu-based catalysts.

props.name: Claim: The review states that bimetallic design addresses the linear scaling…

evidence.quote: strength of intermediates by tuning the d-band center energy level of Cu

props.statement: The review states that bimetallic design addresses the linear scaling relation between intermediate adsorption energies, the electronic interaction tuning adsorption strength through the Cu d-band center energy level (after Abild-Pedersen et al., ref. 85).

props.name: Claim: The review states that Cu coordination polymers reach a total C2+ Fara…

evidence.quote: at an industrial current density of 500 mA cm−2

props.statement: The review states that Cu coordination polymers reach a total C2+ Faradaic efficiency at an industrial current density of 500 mA cm−2, resolving the mass-transfer limitation of traditional polymer-modified catalysts (typically below 100 mA cm−2).

props.name: Claim: The review concludes that close-packed Cu (100) facets favor C2 produc…

evidence.quote: The close-packed Cu (100) crystal facets are more favorable for C2 product formation
Cu (111) crystal facets exhibit higher selectivity toward C1 products

props.statement: The review concludes that close-packed Cu (100) facets favor C2 product formation through a low C−C coupling activation energy, while Cu (111) facets show higher selectivity toward C1 products (Hori et al., refs. 114, 117).

props.name: Claim: The review reports theoretical calculations (Li et al., ref. 120) show…

evidence.quote: on Cu (111) crystal facets than on Cu (100) crystal facets

props.statement: The review reports theoretical calculations (Li et al., ref. 120) showing that at high CO coverage the step following *CO dimerization branches toward the C2H4 pathway more readily on Cu (111) than on Cu (100) facets.

props.name: Claim: The review concludes that remaining challenges for Cu-based CO2RR cata…

evidence.quote: with the hydrogen evolution reaction, and an incomplete theoretical understanding

props.statement: The review concludes that remaining challenges for Cu-based CO2RR catalysts include insufficient structural stability, competition with the hydrogen evolution reaction, and an incomplete theoretical understanding of C2+ product formation pathways.

props.name: Claim: The review reports that the electron-donating-group-modified copper ph…

evidence.quote: achieving 100% Faradaic efficiency for CO in Figure 2a

props.statement: The review reports that the electron-donating-group-modified copper phthalocyanine CuPc−NH2 (on CNTs) significantly enhances CO2RR activity over unmodified CuPc, achieving 100% Faradaic efficiency for CO (Fang et al., ref. 52).

props.name: Claim: The review reports that the electron-withdrawing CuPc−F8 promotes the…

evidence.quote: inhibiting CO2 reduction activity and yielding formic
acid as the primary product in Figure 2b

props.statement: The review reports that the electron-withdrawing CuPc−F8 promotes the hydrogen evolution reaction, inhibits CO2 reduction activity and yields formic acid as the primary product (Fang et al., ref. 52).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a donor–acceptor copper porphyrin catalyst (CuTAPP)…

evidence.quote: achieves a high Faradaic efficiency of 54.8% and a partial current density of 290.5 mA cm−2

props.statement: The review reports a donor–acceptor copper porphyrin catalyst (CuTAPP) whose amino donors enrich electron density at the central CuN4 sites, reaching a Faradaic efficiency of 54.8% for CH4 and a partial current density of 290.5 mA cm−2 at −1.63 V (vs RHE) (Yu et al., ref. 54).

props.name: Claim: The review reports an F-doped carbon-supported Cu catalyst (F−Cu/C) wh…

evidence.quote: resulting in 82.5% Faradaic efficiency for C2+ products
at 400 mA·cm−2 and 44 h of stability in Figure 2g

props.statement: The review reports an F-doped carbon-supported Cu catalyst (F−Cu/C) whose electron-deficient support lowers the C−C coupling barrier, giving 82.5% Faradaic efficiency for C2+ products at 400 mA·cm−2 and 44 h of stability (Wang et al., ref. 56).

props.name: Claim: The review reports that in an aminothiol ligand-modified Cu catalyst t…

evidence.quote: lowers the activation energy required for the C−C coupling reaction in Figure 2h

props.statement: The review reports that in an aminothiol ligand-modified Cu catalyst the amino group donates electron density to the copper surface through strong N−Cu bonds, enhancing CO2 activation and lowering the C−C coupling activation energy (Wan et al., ref. 57).

props.name: Claim: The review reports that Sb−S covalent bonds tune the Cu−S bond length…

evidence.quote: of the *HCOO intermediate, enabling a 72% Faradaic efficiency for formic acid

props.statement: The review reports that Sb−S covalent bonds tune the Cu−S bond length in CuS, strengthening *HCOO binding and enabling a 72% Faradaic efficiency for formic acid (Wei et al., ref. 58).

props.name: Claim: The review reports that in Cu2OSO4@CuO the sacrificial electron-withdr…

evidence.quote: This regulation achieves a Faradaic efficiency of 88% for C2+ products.

props.statement: The review reports that in Cu2OSO4@CuO the sacrificial electron-withdrawing agent SO42− is reduced to S2− during CO2RR, downshifting the Cu d-band center and balancing *CO/*COH adsorption, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 88% for C2+ products (Wang et al., ref. 59).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a sterically hindered porphyrin salicylimine Cu com…

evidence.quote: CH4 reaches 84% in Figure 3c

props.statement: The review reports a sterically hindered porphyrin salicylimine Cu complex (o−Cu−Por−Sa) whose hydroxyl-built spatial microenvironment drives the reaction toward protonation, reaching a Faradaic efficiency of 84% for CH4 (Wang et al., ref. 60).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a periodic Cu single-atom catalyst on polymeric car…

evidence.quote: a Faradaic efficiency of 71.1% for CH4
was achieved with a partial current density of 426.6 mA cm−2

props.statement: The review reports a periodic Cu single-atom catalyst on polymeric carbon nitride (Cu1/PCN) with low-valence Cuδ+ centers in a diagonal N−Cu−N configuration, whose steric arrangement inhibits C−C coupling, reaching a Faradaic efficiency of 71.1% for CH4 and a partial current density of 426.6 mA cm−2 at −1.50 V (vs. RHE) (Feng et al., ref. 61).

props.name: Claim: The review reports Cu2O nanoparticles grafted with long-chain alkyl ca…

evidence.quote: a Faradaic efficiency for C2H4 exceeding 63.0% on the

props.statement: The review reports Cu2O nanoparticles grafted with long-chain alkyl carboxylic acids (C4−C18), where confined *CO diffusion raises local CO concentration and promotes multi-carbon products, with a Faradaic efficiency for C2H4 exceeding 63.0% on the C12/C18−Cu2O catalyst (Li et al., ref. 62).

props.name: Claim: The review reports homogeneous Cu nanoclusters (Cu13 and Cu14) in whic…

evidence.quote: achieving deep reduction to hydrocarbon
products at −1.2 V (vs. RHE).

props.statement: The review reports homogeneous Cu nanoclusters (Cu13 and Cu14) in which the Cu14 surface lowers the *COOH adsorption energy, enabling deep reduction to hydrocarbon products at −1.2 V (vs. RHE) (Han et al., ref. 63).

props.name: Claim: The review reports octadecyl-chain-grafted Cu nanowires whose long alk…

evidence.quote: ultimately achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 53% for C2H4.

props.statement: The review reports octadecyl-chain-grafted Cu nanowires whose long alkyl chains modulate *CO adsorption and suppress HER through hydrophobicity, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 53% for C2H4 (Li et al., ref. 64).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a Cu−Pd alloy in which Pd atoms sterically block C−…

evidence.quote: of 43.23% for CH4

props.statement: The review reports a Cu−Pd alloy in which Pd atoms sterically block C−C coupling and adsorb *H to promote *CO hydrogenation, realizing a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 43.23% for CH4 (Huang et al., ref. 65).

props.name: Claim: The review reports Cu porphyrin immobilized on multi-walled carbon nan…

evidence.quote: enables a Faradaic efficiency of 37.3% for CH4 with effective HER suppression

props.statement: The review reports Cu porphyrin immobilized on multi-walled carbon nanotubes, where the ultra-thin porphyrin layer restricts *CO diffusion and stabilizes coexisting Cu2+ and Cu0, enabling a Faradaic efficiency of 37.3% for CH4 with effective HER suppression (Esfandiari et al., ref. 66).

props.name: Claim: The review reports (computationally) that endohedral 3d/4d dopants in…

evidence.quote: potential for the CO2RR by approximately 20% compared to pure Cu13 clusters

props.statement: The review reports (computationally) that endohedral 3d/4d dopants in XCu12 bimetallic clusters induce steric rearrangement of surface Cu atoms, reducing the CO2 activation energy and lowering the CO2RR overpotential by approximately 20% relative to pure Cu13 clusters (Mohanta et al., ref. 67).

props.name: Claim: The review reports Cu2−xSe nanosheets in which Se-vacancy lattice stre…

evidence.quote: Cu−Cu spacing to 2.51 Å
a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 68.1% for ethanol

props.statement: The review reports Cu2−xSe nanosheets in which Se-vacancy lattice stress shortens the Cu−Cu spacing to 2.51 Å and lowers the C−C coupling barrier, achieving a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 68.1% for ethanol (Wang et al., ref. 68).

conversion to ethanol and a partial current density of 35.6 mA cm−2 at −0.7 V (vs. RHE) in
0.1 M KHCO3 electrolyte saturated with CO2

props.statement: The review reports an ultrahigh-density Cu single-atom catalyst (Cu component 13.35 wt% on thin-walled N-doped carbon nanotubes) whose high-density Cu−N site distribution promotes C−C coupling, giving a Faradaic efficiency of 81.9% for ethanol and a partial current density of 35.6 mA cm−2 at −0.7 V (vs. RHE) in CO2-saturated 0.1 M KHCO3 (Xia et al., ref. 78).

evidence.quote: Faradaic efficiency of 75.4% and a partial current density of 289.2 mA cm−2

props.statement: The review reports a hybrid M−Cu/CuNP catalyst with Cu nanoparticles and atomically dispersed Cu on N-doped carbon, where Cu nanoparticles promote *CHO dimerization and atomic Cu sites accelerate *CO-to-*CHO conversion, achieving a multi-carbon product Faradaic efficiency of 75.4% and a partial current density of 289.2 mA cm−2 (Feng et al., ref. 79).

evidence.quote: the methanol Faradaic efficiencies of Cu−SAs/CNF and
Cu−SAs/TCNF were 41% and 44%, respectively

props.statement: The review reports Cu single-atom catalysts on carbon nanofibers (Cu−SAs/CNF) and tubular carbon nanofibers (Cu−SAs/TCNF) reaching methanol Faradaic efficiencies of 41% and 44%, respectively, at −0.9 V (vs. RHE), the difference arising from distinct Cu–support interactions (Yang et al., ref. 80).

props.name: Claim: The review reports single-atom Cu doped onto CeO2 where each Cu site i…

evidence.quote: each Cu site was accompanied by three oxygen vacancies
58% in Figure 4h

props.statement: The review reports single-atom Cu doped onto CeO2 where each Cu site is accompanied by three oxygen vacancies, constructing CO adsorption and activation centers with excellent methane selectivity, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 58% (Wang et al., ref. 81).

props.name: Claim: The review reports carbon-supported Cu single atoms prepared via a Cu−…

evidence.quote: achieved a Faradaic efficiency of 91% for ethanol production at −0.7 V (vs. RHE) in Figure

props.statement: The review reports carbon-supported Cu single atoms prepared via a Cu−Li composite precursor route that dynamically aggregate into clusters during the reaction, whose synergy with remaining isolated Cu sites facilitates C−C coupling, achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 91% for ethanol at −0.7 V (vs. RHE) (Xu et al., ref. 82).

props.statement: The review reports Pd−Cu bimetallic aerogels (Pd83Cu17) of crystalline Pd nanochains and amorphous Cu, reaching a Faradaic efficiency of 80% for methanol and a partial current density of 31.8 mA cm−2 at −0.8 V (vs. RHE) in 0.1 M KHCO3, with stable operation during 100 h of continuous electrolysis (Lu et al., ref. 87).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a Cu−Sn bimetallic catalyst (Cu1Sn1) in which Sn cr…

props.statement: The review reports a Cu−Sn bimetallic catalyst (Cu1Sn1) in which Sn creates coordination sites for HCOO− adsorption and weakens CO adsorption, giving 92% selectivity for formate with a partial current density of 28.5 mA cm−2 at −0.8 V (vs. RHE) (Zhang et al., ref. 88).

props.name: Claim: The review reports Cu−Bi bimetallic nanostructures in which electron t…

evidence.quote: These surfaces stabilize *OCHO adsorbates and

props.statement: The review reports Cu−Bi bimetallic nanostructures in which electron transfer from Cu to Bi forms electron-enriched bimetallic sites that stabilize *OCHO adsorbates and lower their formation barrier, selectively promoting formate (Li et al., ref. 89).

props.name: Claim: The review reports an Ag−Cu2O heterojunction catalyst (Ag−Cu2O−0.10) w…

evidence.quote: configuration facilitates an ethylene selectivity of 66.0% and a partial current density of

props.statement: The review reports an Ag−Cu2O heterojunction catalyst (Ag−Cu2O−0.10) with partially reduced Cu+/Cu0 interface sites; DFT calculations indicate the interface configuration facilitates an ethylene selectivity of 66.0% and a partial current density of 429.1 mA cm−2 (Wei et al., ref. 90).

props.name: Claim: The review reports the mononuclear Cu coordination polymer Cu(OH)−BTA,…

evidence.quote: achieving a Faradaic efficiency of 73% for total
C2 products and 57% specifically for ethylene

props.statement: The review reports the mononuclear Cu coordination polymer Cu(OH)−BTA, whose spatially adjacent Cu atoms form geometrically compatible dual active sites driving *OCCHO formation; in a flow electrolytic cell at 500 mA cm−2 it reaches a Faradaic efficiency of 73% for total C2 products and 57% specifically for ethylene (Liang et al., ref. 94).

props.name: Claim: The review reports mononuclear Cu coordination polymers built from six…

evidence.quote: ranging from 0.26 to 0.86

props.statement: The review reports mononuclear Cu coordination polymers built from six phenyl-1H-1,2,3-triazole derivatives, where adjusting the ligand HOMO energy level directionally regulates Cu electron density and C−C coupling efficiency over a wide range, with values ranging from 0.26 to 0.86 (Yang et al., ref. 95).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a conjugated Cu phthalocyanine polymer (CuPPc) whos…

evidence.quote: of CH4 reaches 55% with a partial current density of 18 mA cm−2

props.statement: The review reports a conjugated Cu phthalocyanine polymer (CuPPc) whose spatially isolated Cu−N4 sites inhibit C−C coupling and promote *CO protonation; at −1.25 V (vs. RHE) the Faradaic efficiency of CH4 reaches 55% with a partial current density of 18 mA cm−2 (Zhang et al., ref. 96).

props.name: Claim: The review reports electrodeposited bimetallic Cu−Ag foam dendrites in…

evidence.quote: active sites, strengthen CO adsorption, and consequently elevate the current density of

props.statement: The review reports electrodeposited bimetallic Cu−Ag foam dendrites in which introducing Ag changes dendrite size and morphology, increasing specific surface area and roughness; the modifications strengthen CO adsorption and elevate the CO2 reduction current density (Kottakkat et al., ref. 101).

props.name: Claim: The review reports CuxAuy nanowire arrays whose 1D architecture restri…

evidence.quote: highly selective ethanol generation at lower potentials

props.limitations: The review names 'He et al. [103]', but reference 103 in its list is Zhu et al., J. Energy Chem. 2019 (electrodeposited CuxAuy nanowire arrays); not resolved here.
props.statement: The review reports CuxAuy nanowire arrays whose 1D architecture restricts OH− and HCO3− diffusion, raises local pH and the *CO/*H ratio, and reduces CO desorption, collectively enabling highly selective ethanol generation at lower potentials (attributed to He et al., ref. 103).

props.name: Claim: The review reports Cu@Ag core–shell nanoparticles with tunable Ag shel…

evidence.quote: exhibited the highest Faradaic
efficiency of multi-carbon products

props.statement: The review reports Cu@Ag core–shell nanoparticles with tunable Ag shell thickness, where the optimally designed Cu@Ag−2 exhibited the highest Faradaic efficiency for multi-carbon products, attributed to *CO enrichment on the Cu core and higher active-site density (Zhang et al., ref. 104).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a core–shell vacancy-engineered Cu2S−u−V catalyst w…

evidence.quote: achieving a total Faradaic efficiency of 32% for C1 alcohols and 57% for C2H4
stable operation for over 67 h

props.statement: The review reports a core–shell vacancy-engineered Cu2S−u−V catalyst whose sulfur-doped core redirects *CO protonation from ethylene to alcohols; in a flow electrolytic cell at 500 mA cm−2 it achieves a total Faradaic efficiency of 32% for C1 alcohols and 57% for C2H4, and it operates stably for over 67 h in a membrane electrode assembly (Zhuang et al., ref. 107).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a Cu/Cu2O aerogel whose widely distributed Cu0−Cu+…

evidence.quote: exhibited a Faradaic efficiency of 41.2% for ethanol at a partial current density of 32.55 mA

props.statement: The review reports a Cu/Cu2O aerogel whose widely distributed Cu0−Cu+ interfaces and locally raised pH promote CO conversion to ethanol, exhibiting a Faradaic efficiency of 41.2% for ethanol at a partial current density of 32.55 mA cm−2 (Kim et al., ref. 109).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a bicontinuous b−Cu2O/Cu electrocatalyst of ultra-s…

evidence.quote: Faradaic efficiency of 12.1% for CO2 reduction to propanol at −1.1 V (vs. RHE), with a
partial current density of 101.6 mA cm−2

props.statement: The review reports a bicontinuous b−Cu2O/Cu electrocatalyst of ultra-small Cu2O nanodomains, Cu nanodomains and abundant grain boundaries, facilitating *CO formation and coupling, exhibiting a Faradaic efficiency of 12.1% for propanol at −1.1 V (vs. RHE) with a partial current density of 101.6 mA cm−2 (Zhang et al., ref. 110).

props.name: Claim: The review reports electrodeposited CuO nanosheets that reorganize und…

evidence.quote: promote selective formation of C2H4 even at low overpotentials

props.statement: The review reports electrodeposited CuO nanosheets that reorganize under CO2RR into high grain-boundary-density structures whose coordination-unsaturated Cu sites form stable Cu+/Cu0 interfaces, elevating *CO coverage and promoting selective C2H4 formation even at low overpotentials (Zhang et al., ref. 111).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a fluorine-stabilized Cu(I)/Cu(0) core–shell interf…

evidence.quote: achieving a high C2 Faradaic efficiency of 80.2%

props.statement: The review reports a fluorine-stabilized Cu(I)/Cu(0) core–shell interfacial architecture (P−Cux/Cu2OF) whose interface region significantly enhances ethanol production, achieving a high C2 Faradaic efficiency of 80.2% (Cai et al., ref. 112).

props.name: Claim: The review reports a carbon-coated CuOx catalyst (CuOx@C) from one-pot…

evidence.quote: enabling a high C2
Faradaic efficiency of 82%

props.statement: The review reports a carbon-coated CuOx catalyst (CuOx@C) from one-pot pyrolysis of a Cu-based MOF, which preserves the Cuδ+−Cu0 interface and lowers the C−C coupling barrier, enabling a high C2 Faradaic efficiency of 82% (Zang et al., ref. 113).

props.statement: The review reports that among three Cu2O phases the t−Cu2O phase achieves the highest C2H4 selectivity, up to 68%, consistent with DFT showing the Cu2O (100) facet reduces the *CO dimerization energy barrier by 0.3 eV relative to Cu2O (111) (Gao et al., ref. 116).

props.statement: The review reports Ag nanoparticles loaded on Cu catalysts with exposed specific facets as tandem systems: nano-octahedrons exposing Cu (111) are rich in CHx intermediates and favor CH4, while the Ag component provides a high concentration of CO species and promotes alcohol formation via CHx–CO coupling (Iyengar et al., ref. 118).

props.statement: The review reports Ag−Cu heterostructure nanomaterials with dominant exposed Cu (100) facets, grown by site-specific epitaxial deposition on an Ag substrate through adjusted precursor surface activity and reduction kinetics (e.g. Ag65−Cu35 JNS−100(6)) (Ma et al., ref. 119).
